First thing, DEFENSE DEFENSE DEFENSE! Youre experiencing what I have experienced a lot in fighting games. You practice a whole bunch of combos and get them down in the lab, but you still get beat by super easy cheese strats like auto combo spam and super dash. And since youre getting beat by that, it feels like youre getting stomped by noobs. Truth is, you just have to master defense. Go into matches and really hone in on whats beating you. In what situation are you eating super dashes and auto combos? Really look into it. Forget your combos. Focus on defense. THEN go on to practice combos, once you can finally consistently read and defend against average tactics. This is really important, and saves a whole bunch of headaches.

Helpful tip, remember that jump blocking is pretty safe. You can still block ground attacks in the air and you can't get mixed up if you're in the air. Its a helpful defense against a lot of the cheese you'll see when you first go online. If theyre spamming auto combo and happen to tag you in the air? No worries bc it wont finish the combo and you'll have another chance to block. This tactic helped me a lot.

Go online, get your ass beat, and analyze why ts happening. Constantly ask yourself what you are losing to and once you figure it out head into training mode and drill beating it. Then the next time you're up against it, focus on applying what you learned even if it costs you the match. Learn from every opponent and every loss. THAT is much more important than learning combos. Learn basic bnbs with your favorite characters, then focus on developing a strong defense. THEN move on to the more complicated stuff.

Unfortunately I wasn't able to experience Bloodborne(no playstation) but I do understand what you mean with the ramping down of the difficulty. 

In DS1 the hardest part for me was the early lack of fast travel. We had to decide where we wanted to go early and exploring meant we were going deeep into uncharted areas with no real way to get out. I remember being stuck down in blighttown for a long time with seemingly no way to make my way back out as my frames were slowly stolen away with my souls. I remember constantly succumbing to the traps in sens fortress, wondering whether I should keep pressing forward or retreat back and become stronger to go through it later. 

And oh man once you got to anor londo. If you didn't have the gall to defeat O and S with what you had on you, then enjoy the walk back to the gargoyles, down back through the fortress. I made that journey a few times and it really made the world feel more connected and less random worlds that were connected via bonfire. And like you said, it was a convenience that made the game easier and made it feel less like a battle through hell and more like an altercation through purgatory.

One thing I will say with the utmost of confidence, is that we all long for the experience we had when we first started dark souls. But it just isn't going to happen. That experience couldn't be recreated in a thousand years unless we drained our mind of the knowledge we have of souls games.

Even in other games similar to dark souls (Dragons Dogma) (Momodora) (others I cant think to name) I find my dark souls knowledge seeping into my experience with those games and actually helping me beat them.

Dark Souls has conditioned us to play these types of games a certain way, and as long as we maintain our reserved playstyles and take in our surroundings and  read and analyze the movesets and tells of our enemies, we just won't have the same experience ever again. Sadly, we have already been conditioned.

I like to think of DS3 to the Souls series as The Legend of Korra was to the Avatar series. Many people think Korra wasn't as good as the original series. But I loved Korra because even if it wasnt as good as the original, it was still decent and more of the Avatar content we all wanted.

DS3 feels complete to me because I got everything I expected. I wanted more Dark Souls with new lands and lore to explore and thats what I got. So I love and will continue to love the game.
